newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Earthquake shakes Malaysia, north Sumatra.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake shakes Malaysia, north Sumatra.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 6.0 on the Richter scale rocked Indonesia's northern Sumatra island and peninsular Malaysia on Thursday evening, Indonesian government officials said on Friday.
There were no reports of casualties or damage.

The Meteorological and Geophysics Office in Jakarta said the quake struck at 10.20 p.m. (1520 GMT) and was centred in the Indian Ocean off the coast of Sumatra, some 1,500 km (930 miles) northwest of the capital.
The agency had earlier said the epicentre was on land, some 67 km (40 miles) north of the Sumatran coastal town of Tapaktuan.
Seismologists in Hong Kong and Australia also recorded the quake and put its strength at six on the Richter scale.
Residents in major north Sumatran cities including Medan, Banda Aceh, Tapaktuan and Kutacane said they felt the tremors but had not heard of any casualties.
"We felt the quake strongly and we saw people running out from houses late in the evening," one government official at the ministry of information in Tapaktuan told Reuters.
"But we haven't received any report of damages or casualties at present," the official said.
A telecommunication employee in Kutacane said fresh tremors were registered on Friday morning.
Harian Analisa, the local paper for northern Sumatran area, said people fled their homes in Medan, the capital of north Sumatra, after the tremor.
It said residents had flocked into Medan's main streets on fears that aftershocks may rock the area.
Tremors also shook parts of western peninsular Malaysia, including the capital Kuala Lumpur, causing residents to flee their homes, the Malaysian national Bernama news agency reported.
There were no reports of damage or casualties from the tremors, which lasted several seconds, it said.
Bernama quoted a police spokesman as saying that the quake caused power supply disruptions in several areas.
"Residents of several high-rise buildings, including flats, rushed out when they felt the tremors," he said.
